log.title: 10-year edge tests: can filters lift R per trade?
log.question: Do breakout volume, an RS-line high, base depth, a stop cap or pyramiding move the system from +0.2R towards +0.4R?
log.setup: Current rules (top theme, 10-day-low stop, ⅓ day 3 + 10-day trail), 0.5% risk, 8 positions; one change at a time.
log.result: Current: $195k, +7.3%/yr, +0.20R. Add ½ on the first 10-day pullback: $197k, +7.5%/yr, +0.20R (neutral). Base depth ≥ 20%: +5.2%/yr, +0.15R. RS-line high: +3.8%/yr, +0.10R. Skip stops > 8%: +3.3%/yr, +0.09R, DD −27%. Breakout volume ≥ 1.5× (buy at the close): +1.5%/yr, +0.09R. Combinations were worse.
log.verdict: No mechanical filter beyond the theme filter improved the edge; wide stops are part of why it works. The path from 0.2R to 0.3–0.4R is discretionary: chart selection, entry precision and discipline, which daily-bar backtests can't measure. Track it live.

log.title: 10-year sizing test
log.question: With ~60% of the account idle, does more risk per trade or more positions close the gap with buy-and-hold?
log.setup: Best 10-year rules (top theme, 10-day-low stop, ⅓ day 3 + 10-day trail); risk 0.5 / 0.75 / 1%, 8 or 12 positions.
log.result: Base (0.5% risk, 8 positions): $189k, +6.9%/yr, DD −19%. 0.75% risk: $248k, +10.1%/yr, DD −27%. 1% risk: $316k, +12.9%/yr, DD −32%. 0.75% risk, 12 positions: $361k, +14.6%/yr, DD −34%. 1% risk, 12 positions: $436k, +16.9%/yr, DD −35%, beat RSP in 7 of 10 years. RSP: $288k, +11.8%/yr, DD −39%.
log.verdict: More risk per trade and more positions scale the edge almost proportionally. 0.75–1% risk with up to 12 positions beats buy-and-hold with a slightly smaller drawdown; pick the level whose −30 to −35% drawdown you can sit through.

log.title: 10-year rule tests
log.question: Which rules hold up across bull, bear and choppy markets?
log.setup: 14 full $100k books, one rule changed at a time, 0.5% risk, 8 positions.
log.result: 10-day-low stop: $194k, +7.3%/yr, max DD −20%, worst year −3%, 7/10 up years, +0.20R/trade. Prior-day-low stop: $121k, +2.1%/yr, DD −38%. Every market gate lowered returns (RSP > 50-day: −2.7%/yr); risk gauges cut DD to −25%. No theme filter: $33k. 20-day trail, ⅓ at 2R and fixed 20-day exits all worse than ⅓ day 3 + 10-day trail. Re-run on the 10-day-low stop: RSP > 200-day gate $157k, +5.0%/yr, DD −16%, 8/10 up years; RS ≥ 90 DD −15%; risk gauges 9/10 up years but +4.1%/yr.
log.verdict: Keep: top theme, 10-day-low stop, ⅓ on day 3 + 10-day trail. Market gauges for sizing, not on/off. The tighter stop from R5 was reversed.

log.title: 10-year backtest, $100k
log.question: What would $100k have done over a decade?
log.setup: Top-theme setups, prior-day-low stop, ⅓ day 3 + 10-day trail, 0.5% risk, 8 positions, today's universe (survivorship bias).
log.verdict: The mechanical signal alone is not an edge over a decade; the 18-month results were a favourable window.

log.title: $100k portfolio, last 18 months
log.question: What does the strategy look like as a real account?
log.setup: Top-theme setups, prior-day-low stop, 0.5% risk, max 8 positions, compounding.
log.result: $100k → $154k (+34%/yr, DD −13.6%) vs RSP +27%. Without the theme filter: $80k (−19.5%).
log.verdict: Strong, but a single favourable period — superseded by R7/R8.

log.title: Loss control (18 months)
log.question: Can losses be made smaller in R?
log.setup: Top-theme setups, ⅓ day 3 + 10-day trail; stop and exit variants.
log.result: Prior-day-low stop (5.7% wide vs 10%): +0.30R/trade vs +0.24R. 1-ATR stop: +0.02R. Failed-breakout exit: +0.03R. Day-5 time stop: avg loss −0.63R but +0.22R/trade.
log.verdict: Reversed by R8: over 10 years the tight stop got shaken out; the 10-day-low stop is better.

log.title: Gate test (18 months)
log.question: Which filters add edge to the setups?
log.setup: Day-3 rule, max 3 new trades a day.
log.result: Top-8 theme: +0.24R/trade vs +0.13R baseline. ADR ≥ 4%: +0.15R, smaller DD. RSP > 50-day, risk gauges, breadth, RS ≥ 90: all lower R/trade.
log.verdict: Theme filter confirmed by R8; market gates confirmed as not adding return.

log.title: Selling rules (18 months)
log.question: How many R do the setups earn with real selling rules?
log.setup: Same entries; fixed 20-day vs ⅓ day 3 + 10-day trail vs ⅓ at 2R + 20-day trail.
log.result: Day-3 rule: +66R closed + 59R open; 21 trades ≥ 5R made +215R, the rest lost ~150R. ⅓ at 2R: lowest per-trade result.
log.verdict: Profits come from a few big winners; don't sell everything early. Confirmed by R8.

log.title: Setup tracker, fixed exit (12 months)
log.question: Does the SETUP shape work with a mechanical 20-day exit?
log.setup: Pivot break entry, 10-day-low stop, exit after 20 days.
log.result: Win 42%, avg win +1.2R, avg loss −0.9R, ~0R per trade; 16% ever reached +2R. SETUP +0.5% over 20 days vs +1.6% for any RS 80+ stock.
log.verdict: The shape alone adds little; the selling rule matters more.

log.title: Model book: what big winners had in common
log.question: Which traits made a breakout more likely to double?
log.setup: 25,327 breakouts, 491 went on to double (base rate 2.8%).
log.result: ADR ≥ 4%: 3.3× the base rate · deep base 3.3× · RS ≥ 90: 3.1× · episodic pivot 2.6× · SETUP 1.8× · tight 1.1× · within 15% of the 52-week high 0.76×.
log.verdict: Volatility and strong relative strength matter; tightness on its own does little.
